discovery_sources: A-Islands frozen original and strong-reference outputs

primary_hypothesis.name: extreme_isolation_topology_interaction
primary_hypothesis.statement: After a strong ecological reference is supplied, the incremental held-out effect of a species-conditioned structural coordinate becomes more favourable in the extreme-isolation tail than in the remaining eligible spatial units.
primary_hypothesis.increment_definition: candidate held-out loss minus strong-reference held-out loss; negative is favourable
primary_hypothesis.moderator: one response-independent isolation metric selected from system biology before any pilot or confirmatory response access
primary_hypothesis.extreme_isolation_rule: upper 25% of the frozen eligible-unit isolation distribution, computed from predictor-only data before response access
primary_hypothesis.primary_contrast: mean candidate-minus-reference loss in extreme-isolation units minus mean candidate-minus-reference loss in non-extreme units

minimum_components: spatial unit area or size when ecologically meaningful
a process-aware or source-aware isolation representation appropriate to the system

presence_absence_asymmetry.statement: Test whether the topology increment differs between true presences and true absences.

range_source_breadth.statement: Estimate the continuous interaction between pre-response species range/source breadth and topology increment.
range_source_breadth.expected_direction_from_discovery: broader source sets may increase topology redundancy outside extreme isolation

transfer_design.cross_origin_claim_rule: a shared island-fragmentation claim requires the primary extreme-isolation interaction to retain the same direction under spatial transfer in independently admitted systems

anti_selection: do not choose a future system because exploratory subgroup results already look favourable
do not choose the isolation metric after inspecting future responses
do not move the 75% threshold after response access
do not remove non-extreme spatial units after response access
do not select taxa using within-system candidate-minus-reference direction
do not use A-Islands or Tanzania exploratory subgroup statistics in the future confirmatory denominator
do not call presence-versus-absence subgroup success the primary result

claim_ceiling.if_primary_supported_under_local_and_spa: topology retains incremental predictive information preferentially under extreme isolation beyond the declared strong reference in the tested systems
not_licensed: extreme isolation causes the topology effect
the 75% threshold is universal across ecosystems
one common dispersal mechanism applies to islands and fragments
